cuts.raw_narration: In a quiet bedroom, the spiky black-haired boy with a bandage on his forehead sits up with his arm in a sling, listening to the tall examiner in the dark suit and curled purple mustache. When the boy asks who ended up failing the Hunter exam, the examiner pauses and quietly answers: Killua. The boy freezes, stunned.

The examiner walks him through what he missed. In the arena, a hunched fighter's face is bristling with long needles — a hand pulls them out one by one and the disguise falls away, revealing a tall young man with long straight black hair and flat, pupil-less black eyes. The white-haired boy stares in dread as this stranger calmly speaks to him with the eerie flatness of family.

Standing across the arena floor, the long-haired brother tells the white-haired boy he is not cut out to be a Hunter — he was born to be an assassin. The camera cuts to his tilted head and black, empty eyes, and to the white-haired boy standing rigid under the pressure.

Cornered, the white-haired boy suddenly shouts back — there IS something he wants: he wants to be friends with the boy in the sling. He says he is sick of killing people; he just wants to have fun. The long-haired brother's face does not change.

The long-haired brother then says, calmly: fine — I'll just kill him. He turns to leave the ring, the suited man with glasses erupts at the referee, and the white-haired boy stands frozen, sweat running down his face.

Back in the arena, the suited man with glasses and the blond boy shout at the white-haired boy to fight, promising to protect him. But the white-haired boy, staring at the floor, raises his hand and quietly says: you win. I admit defeat.

Later, when the next match begins, there is a blur of motion across the arena. The white-haired boy has crossed the floor in an instant; blood is on his hand and face, and his opponent lies motionless behind him. The examiners react in shock, and the mustached examiner's voice-over notes that just like that, the committee disqualified him.

Back in the bedroom, the boy in the sling has finished listening. His face slowly hardens as the examiner explains that his older brother trampled on the white-haired boy's wish to be a friend and sent him into despair. The camera closes in on the boy in the sling — he is not just upset. He is furious.
